name: Panax ginseng (Asian ginseng)
short: Trial adverse events were similar to placebo (headache, sleep, gut upset). Possible warfarin, phenelzine and alcohol interactions are reported; two small trials found no significant INR difference.
text: A systematic review of adverse effects and drug interactions found that, in clinical trials, adverse events with products containing only Panax ginseng were about as frequent as with placebo; the most common were headache, sleep and gastrointestinal disorders. More serious events appear in isolated case reports and spontaneous reports, where causality is often difficult to determine, and combination products containing ginseng have been associated with serious adverse events and even fatalities, although other ingredients may have been responsible. The same review noted possible drug interactions with warfarin, phenelzine and alcohol. Against this, a small randomised open-label trial in 25 people with ischaemic stroke found that taking Panax ginseng with warfarin did not change warfarin's effect on clotting tests, and a randomised crossover trial of Korean red ginseng in 25 people with heart valve replacements on warfarin found no statistically significant difference in INR changes compared with placebo, while still advising close monitoring.
